topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: The Virginia Real Estate Board is composed of how many members, and how many of them must have been actively engaged as licensed real estate brokers or salespersons for at least seven consecutive years before appointment?
choice_a: Nine members total, seven of whom must have that experience
choice_b: Seven members total, five of whom must have that experience
choice_c: Nine members total, all nine of whom must have that experience
choice_d: Five members total, three of whom must have that experience
explanation: The Board has nine members: seven who have been actively engaged as licensed real estate brokers or salespersons for at least seven consecutive years, plus two citizen members.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: What is the term length for a member of the Virginia Real Estate Board?
choice_a: Two years
choice_b: Four years
choice_c: Five years
choice_d: Six years
explanation: The terms of Board members are four years.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2105, an applicant for an initial license as a real estate salesperson must complete a course in the principles of real estate carrying at least how many hours of classroom, correspondence, or distance-learning instruction?
choice_a: At least 30 hours
choice_b: At least 45 hours
choice_c: At least 60 hours
choice_d: At least 75 hours
explanation: The course must carry academic credit of at least four semester hours, but not less than 60 hours of instruction.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: An applicant for an initial license as a real estate broker must complete not less than how many semester hours of real estate instruction?
choice_a: 4 semester hours
choice_b: 8 semester hours
choice_c: 16 semester hours
choice_d: 12 semester hours
explanation: A broker applicant must complete not less than 12 semester hours of classroom, correspondence, or distance-learning instruction in real estate courses.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2105.01, a new salesperson must complete a post-licensure educational curriculum of at least how many hours within the first year of licensure, and what happens if it is not completed?
choice_a: 30 hours; the license is placed on inactive status until the curriculum is completed
choice_b: 15 hours; the license is automatically revoked
choice_c: 60 hours; the licensee must retake the salesperson exam
choice_d: 30 hours; a civil penalty of $500 is imposed
explanation: Failure to complete the 30-hour post-licensure curriculum within one year of license issuance results in the license being placed on inactive status until completed.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2105.03, how many hours of continuing education must an active broker complete during each licensing term, and how many of the total must be required hours including ethics?
choice_a: 16 total hours, with 11 required hours including 3 hours of ethics
choice_b: 24 total hours, with 11 required hours including 3 hours of ethics
choice_c: 24 total hours, with 8 required hours including 2 hours of ethics
choice_d: 30 total hours, with 15 required hours including 5 hours of ethics
explanation: Brokers must complete not less than 24 hours per licensing term: a minimum of 11 required hours (including 3 hours of ethics and standards of conduct, 2 hours of fair housing, 2 hours of legal updates, 2 hours of agency, and 2 hours of contracts), 8 hours on supervision/management, and 5 elective hours.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: How many continuing education hours must an active salesperson (not a broker) complete during each licensing term?
choice_a: 8 hours
choice_b: 24 hours
choice_c: 16 hours
choice_d: 32 hours
explanation: Salespersons must complete not less than 16 hours per licensing term: 11 required hours (same categories as brokers, minus supervision) plus 5 elective hours.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: If a Virginia real estate license has been inactive for more than three years, what does the Board require before it can be reactivated?
choice_a: Nothing; inactive licenses reactivate automatically upon request
choice_b: A new criminal background check only
choice_c: Re-taking and passing the salesperson exam only, with no education requirement
choice_d: Remedial educational requirements meeting the standards in effect at the time the license becomes active (unless a waiver condition applies)
explanation: Board regulations require remedial education meeting current standards, though the Board may waive this in specific circumstances (e.g. an occupation that retained real estate knowledge, or certain military-spouse situations).

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2105.2, what is the maximum civil penalty the Board may impose on a person engaging in unlicensed real estate activity after a cease-and-desist order, per transaction?
choice_a: $1,000, or the compensation received from the transaction, whichever is greater
explanation: The Board may impose a civil penalty not to exceed $1,000 per transaction or the compensation received, whichever is greater; penalties are paid to the Literary Fund.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2106.1, can an individual holding a broker's license operate a real estate brokerage firm as a sole proprietorship without further licensure?
choice_a: No, a separate firm license is always required
choice_b: Yes, provided the individual does not operate the firm under a fictitious name
choice_c: Yes, but only if the firm operates under a fictitious name
choice_d: Only if the individual has held the broker's license for at least 5 years
explanation: A broker may operate a sole-proprietorship brokerage firm without further licensure, but may not operate it under a fictitious name (a non-broker-owned sole proprietorship must still obtain a Board license).

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: If a principal broker dies or becomes disabled, for how many days may another licensed broker be designated to carry on the business solely to conclude the designating broker's business?
choice_a: Up to 30 days
choice_b: Up to 90 days
choice_c: Up to 180 days
choice_d: Up to one year
explanation: A broker's requirement to designate another licensed broker to carry on the business for up to 180 days applies in the event of the designating broker's death or disability.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2110.1, how long must a supervising broker maintain the records demonstrating reasonable and adequate supervision, and to whom must they be furnished upon request?
choice_a: One year; furnished to the client
choice_b: Seven years; furnished to the IRS
choice_c: Five years; furnished to the local circuit court
choice_d: Three years; furnished to the Board's agent
explanation: Supervising brokers must maintain the required supervision records for three years, furnished to the Board's agent upon request.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: A supervising broker who resides more than how many miles from a supervised branch office must certify quarterly, in writing, that he has complied with the supervision requirements?
choice_a: 50 miles
choice_b: 25 miles
choice_c: 75 miles
choice_d: 100 miles
explanation: A supervising broker residing more than 50 miles from a supervised branch office must certify quarterly compliance on a Board-provided form.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-13, if a licensing fee is submitted to the Board, how is it treated?
choice_a: Refundable within 30 days if the application is withdrawn
choice_b: Nonrefundable and not prorated
choice_c: Prorated based on the remaining license term
choice_d: Held in escrow until the license is approved
explanation: All fees are nonrefundable and will not be prorated; the date of receipt by the board or its agent determines timeliness.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-65 (Universal License Recognition), what may the Board issue to an individual who holds an equivalent license in good standing in a neighboring state?
choice_a: A temporary 90-day permit only
choice_b: Automatic Virginia licensure with no application required
choice_c: A salesperson or broker license under universal license recognition, upon meeting the qualifications
choice_d: Nothing; Virginia does not recognize any other state's license
explanation: Universal license recognition allows the Board to issue a Virginia salesperson or broker license to a qualifying individual licensed in a neighboring state.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: In order to be active as a broker in more than one firm at the same time under 18VAC135-20-50, what must a broker obtain?
choice_a: A single license that automatically covers all firms
choice_b: This is not permitted under any circumstances
choice_c: Written permission from the Board only, no additional license needed
choice_d: Concurrent licenses, approved by the principal broker of each firm
explanation: A broker must obtain concurrent licenses by submitting a concurrent license application approved by the principal broker of each firm.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-181, what must the name on a firm's escrow account match?
choice_a: The name by which the firm or sole proprietorship is licensed
choice_b: The individual name of the principal broker
choice_c: Any name the firm chooses for marketing purposes
choice_d: The name of the bank issuing the account
explanation: The escrow account must be in the name by which the firm or sole proprietorship is licensed.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-181, how must escrow accounts, checks, and bank statements be labeled?
choice_a: "Trust" only
choice_b: "Escrow," and the accounts must be designated as "escrow" accounts with the financial institution
choice_c: "Client Funds" only
choice_d: No specific label is required, only internal recordkeeping
explanation: All such accounts, checks, and bank statements must be labeled 'escrow' and designated as escrow accounts with the financial institution.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-181, funds that will ultimately belong to the licensee may be kept in the escrow account provided that withdrawals occur at intervals of not more than how often, so this does not constitute commingling?
choice_a: Every 30 days
choice_b: Every 90 days
choice_c: Every six months
choice_d: Every 12 months
explanation: Periodic withdrawal of licensee-owned funds at intervals of not more than six months, with accurate identification of amounts, avoids a commingling violation.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-181, a licensee may not disburse money from an escrow account unless what condition is met?
choice_a: The disbursement is under $500
choice_b: The disbursement occurs on the first business day of the month
choice_c: The principal broker verbally approves each disbursement
choice_d: Sufficient money is on deposit in that account to the credit of the individual client or property involved
explanation: A licensee must not disburse or cause to be disbursed moneys from an escrow account unless sufficient money is on deposit to the credit of the specific client or property.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: In a property management context, application deposits, security deposits, and rent paid to a licensee acting for a landlord must be deposited into an escrow account in accordance with which statute?
choice_b: VA Code 54.1-2138
choice_c: VA Code 54.1-2130
choice_d: VA Code 54.1-2100
explanation: Application deposits, security deposits, rent, or other money paid to a licensee acting on behalf of a landlord must be deposited into an escrow account per VA Code 54.1-2108.1.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-30, what is a required qualification for every applicant for an individual salesperson or broker license?
choice_a: A college degree in any field
choice_b: Requirements established by the Board, applicable to all applicants
choice_c: At least 21 years of age
choice_d: Five years of prior work experience in any field
explanation: 18VAC135-20-30 sets the qualifications every applicant for an individual salesperson or broker license must have.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-70, how may an inactive licensee activate that license with a licensed real estate firm or sole proprietorship?
choice_a: By verbal notice to the Board
choice_b: Automatically after one year of inactivity
choice_c: By completing an activation form prescribed by the Board
choice_d: Only by retaking the licensing exam
explanation: An inactive licensee may activate the license by completing an activation form prescribed by the Board.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-140, what must all applicants for reinstatement meet in order to reinstate a lapsed license?
choice_a: Only payment of a late fee, no education requirement
choice_b: Nothing further is required for reinstatement
choice_c: A new background check only
choice_d: The applicable education requirements in 18VAC135-20-95 or 18VAC135-20-101
explanation: All applicants for reinstatement must meet the applicable education requirements referenced in the regulation.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-160, what must every principal broker have readily available to the public at the primary place of business?
choice_a: Specific items required by the regulation to be readily available to the public
choice_b: A copy of the firm's tax returns
choice_c: A notarized copy of every licensee's diploma
choice_d: The personal home address of every affiliated licensee
explanation: 18VAC135-20-160 requires every principal broker to have specified items readily available to the public in the primary place of business.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-165, in addition to the duties in VA Code 54.1-2110.1, what must supervising brokers do?
choice_a: Nothing additional; the statute is exhaustive
choice_b: Comply with additional specific duties set out in the regulation
choice_c: Only supervise licensees who work in the same building
choice_d: Personally review every transaction before closing
explanation: 18VAC135-20-165 imposes additional specific duties on supervising brokers beyond those in VA Code 54.1-2110.1.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-105 through the regulation's history notes, what happened to the prior version of the continuing-education renewal rule (former 18VAC135-20-105)?
choice_a: It remains in force unchanged
choice_b: It was renumbered but never repealed
choice_c: It was repealed, effective November 1, 2015
choice_d: It only applies to brokers, not salespersons
explanation: The regulation's historical notes show former 18VAC135-20-105 was repealed effective November 1, 2015.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2105.03(A)(3), what continuing education topic became a required one-time three-hour course for relicensure as of July 1, 2012?
choice_a: Property management calculations
choice_b: Commercial lease negotiation
choice_c: Federal tax law updates
choice_d: Changes to residential standard agency under Article 3 (54.1-2130 et seq.)
explanation: As of July 1, 2012, every applicant for relicensure must complete at least one three-hour continuing education course on the changes to residential standard agency effective July 1, 2011.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2105.03, may military personnel called to active duty receive extra time to complete continuing education requirements?
choice_a: Yes, they may complete the required continuing education within six months of release from active duty
choice_b: No, the deadline is never extended
choice_c: Yes, but only if they submit a request within 10 days of being called to duty
choice_d: Only officers, not enlisted personnel, receive this extension
explanation: Military personnel called to active duty may complete required continuing education within six months of release from active duty.

topic: Licensing, Qualifications, Continuing Education & Escrow Accounts
question: Under VA Code 54.1-2105.03(D), under what circumstances may the Board grant exemptions or waive/reduce continuing education hours?
choice_a: Never; there are no exceptions
choice_b: In cases of certified illness or undue hardship as demonstrated to the Board
choice_c: Only for licensees over age 65
choice_d: Only during a declared state of emergency
explanation: The Board may grant exemptions or waive/reduce continuing education hours in cases of certified illness or undue hardship.
